If you've been missing the ability to double-click the Digital Crown to open the App Switcher on Apple Watch from before watchOS 27, we have good news: the feature appears to be making a comeback in watchOS 27.2 beta 2. Here's what you need to know.

Apple is working to bring back the watchOS App Switcher

Apple today pushed watchOS 27.2 beta 2 out to developers, less than a week after the previous beta 1 release.

Among today's beta release is one small feature that should make longtime Apple Watch users happy, including my colleague Zac Hall. Earlier this month, he wrote about how watchOS 27 removed the ability to double-click the Digital Crown to quickly switch between recently used apps.

In that article, he noted that users were no longer able to quickly jump between recently used apps, and expressed hope that Apple would restore the gesture either before watchOS 27's official release or in an update thereafter.

While Apple hasn't restored the Digital Crown shortcut to the App Switcher in today's watchOS 27.2 beta 2, it has brought the App Switcher back via a new gesture.

According to a discovery in the Apple Den Discord server, shared on X by user Bones, watchOS 27.2 beta 2 allows users to invoke the App Switcher by long-pressing on the bottom of the screen while using an app.

As Bones noted in his post, the App Switcher essentially behaves as it did before: once a user long-presses at the bottom of the screen to bring up the App Switcher, they can scroll through their recently used apps with the Digital Crown, or swipe left on an app and tap the 'X' button to remove it from the switcher.

As with any beta, we can't guarantee this particular gesture will make it into the final release (which is expected next month), but its presence in watchOS 27.2 beta 2 does seem to suggest that Apple is listening to users and actively working on a way to bring the App Switcher back.

Have you missed the App Switcher in watchOS 27? Let us know down in the comments.
